chapter: Arrangements, repertoire and the last band
title: Sadie, the Fosters and a run of tunes he played
summary: A short exchange about the drummer married to Billy's sister, followed by Laurent reeling off waltzes and popular songs from his books.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: Is Sadie the one who was married to Chynee once, the Foster, the drummer, you know, Abby Foster, is that his name? Wasn't she married? One of the Billy's sisters was married to a drummer. He used to play with Celestan.
Chynee. Played with Celestan, yeah. Nancy, September in the Rain, Beautiful Dreamer. Remember of you, that's another one of mine.
Well, that was your number. A waltz.

Yeah. Now is the hour. Bluebird. One, two, three, four, jump. I want to be loved but by only you. Pretending who's on the other side. June 9th, why do I always remember? Beautiful. Beautiful blue Danube. You can't be true. Till the end of time.
There's silver threads among the gold.
Yeah. Yeah, I got them. Yeah, see, I had to use so much paper, I had to write on both sides. Use so much paper. Forever and ever.
Four numbers on one sheet that way.

Aunt Laurie. Scotch tune. That's Scotch number. What'll I do? Oh, man. We used to... Seems like... Pretending. Don't be afraid to come home. The stars will remember. So will I. How soon? I'll dance at your wedding. Manana The little street where old friends meet Boosh, New Orleans
